findings.title: Real personal & business PII committed to public/ and served unauthenticated
findings.evidence: public/backup-replication-fixture.json:8 |   "user_profiles": [{ "id": "workspace", "full_name": "Brian Kiarie Ngugi", "company_name": "RayElite Ltd", "phone": "0758034649", "city": "Kerugoya", "county": "Kirinyaga", "address": "773-10300", "currency": "KES", "timezone": "Africa/Nairobi" }], | public/backup-replication-fixture.json:9 |   "properties": [{ "id": "fixture-property-001", "name": "RayElite Court", "address": "773-10300", "city": "Kerugoya", "county": "Kirinyaga", ... | public/backup-replication-fixture.json:10
findings.impact: — `public/` is served by Next.js with **no authentication**: `GET https://<host>/backup-replication-fixture.json` returns the file to any anonymous visitor or scraper, and it is indexed by search engines. It contains the founder's full legal name, business name, mobile number, street address, town and county (`RayElite Ltd`, `773-10300`, `Kerugoya`, `Kirinyaga`, `0758034649` — the same number published as the support line in `lib/brand.ts:6`), plus two tenant names with mobile numbers and a vendor name with a mobile number. The file is *named* like a test fixture and is *linked* as "Download t
findings.fix: 1. `git rm --cached public/backup-replication-fixture.json`, replace with a genuinely empty template (`{"schema_version":11,"app_version":"fixture","generated_at":"","user":{"id":"workspace"},"counts":{},"data":{}}`) and regenerate the non-PII fields at request time instead of shipping a static file. 2. Move the file out of `public/` (e.g. `fixtures/backup-replication-fixture.json`) and serve it from an authenticated route, or delete the link at `components/backup-manager.tsx:228` entirely. 3. Scrub the founder's phone/address from the fixture, and rotate anything that ever lived in it. ---
findings.fix_notes: public/backup-replication-fixture.json was scrubbed: the founder's full legal name, street address and the tenant/vendor rows are replaced with clearly synthetic demo values and a _notice field. The support phone and company name are intentionally public (lib/brand.ts) and were left alone.

findings.title: documents Storage bucket is created public = true; every tenant document is served from a public URL
findings.evidence: -- supabase-setup/01-create-tables.sql:324-328 | -- 12.  STORAGE BUCKET FOR DOCUMENTS | -- ===================================================================== | INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public) | VALUES ('documents', 'documents', true)
findings.impact: — the `documents` bucket holds **tenant documents**: national-ID / KYC scans, signed leases, receipts, damage photos and property photos (`app/api/documents/route.ts:4-18` accepts `tenant_id` and `document_type`; the dashboard's tenant record is explicitly advertised as storing "Contact, ID and KYC document storage" — `lib/content/marketing.ts:63`). Because the bucket is `public = true`, the `storage.objects` RLS policies created a few lines later (`01-create-tables.sql:336-348`, `02-add-missing-columns.sql:69-86`) are **bypassed for reads** — a public bucket serves objects to anyone who has t
findings.fix: 1. Set the bucket private: `UPDATE storage.buckets SET public = false WHERE id = 'documents';` and change the migration files to `VALUES ('documents', 'documents', false)` — add a new numbered patch (`supabase-setup/21-private-documents-bucket.sql`) rather than editing an already-applied migration, and register it in `PATCH_LOG` (`lib/system.ts:79`). 2. Stop returning `getPublicUrl()`. Return the storage **path**, and serve downloads through an authenticated route that calls `supabase.storage.from("documents").createSignedUrl(path, 600)` — `lib/storage.ts:59-68` already implements exactly this for the `backups` bucket. 3. Migrate already-uploaded objects: re-upload each `documents.file_url` object into the private bucket and rewrite the column to the path form. 4. Rotate/revoke any documen
findings.fix_notes: Duplicate of CRYPTO-005 / INFRA-013. The documents Storage bucket is created private, the policies are owner-scoped, and every read goes through a short-lived owner-bound signed URL. The live project still needs the bucket flipped by hand — runbook section 6.

findings.title: .gitignore gaps: no env template can be committed, and DB dumps / public backups are not excluded
findings.evidence: .gitignore:19  # env files | .gitignore:20  .env* | lib/storage.ts:9-10 |  * If Supabase Storage isn't configured, we fall back to a public |  * edge-cached file under /public/backups (dev mode only).
findings.impact: — `.env*` is a correct and effective block for `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.production` (verified with `git check-ignore`), but the glob also swallows `.env.example` / `.env.sample`, so the repo has **no way to publish an env template**: 30 variables are read by the app (`lib/db/neon.ts:26`, `lib/mpesa/daraja.ts:51-56`, `lib/stripe.ts:7`, `lib/supabase/service.ts:17`, `lib/api/with-db-auth.ts:30`, `app/api/cron/run/route.ts:22`, `app/api/backup/auto/route.ts:27`, `app/api/mpesa/callback/route.ts:29`, `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:7`, `app/api/geocode`/`app/api/properties/[id]/geocode/route.t
findings.fix: ``` # env files — keep the block, but allow the template .env* !.env.example # database dumps / exports that must never be committed *.dump *.backup *.sql.gz /backups/ /public/backups/ /public/*.json.bak ``` Add a committed `env.example` listing all 30 variables with placeholder values (`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=your-service-role-key`) and mark each as server-only or `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, plus a "required in production" flag. Also add `public/backups/` to the ignore list now, before the `lib/storage.ts` fallback is ever exercised. --- # Scope B — Data leaks in responses and logs

findings.title: Nine endpoints console.log raw PII (emails, names, free-text bodies)
findings.evidence: // app/api/newsletter/route.ts:25 |     console.info("[newsletter] subscribe", parsed.data)          // { email, source } | // app/api/pricing/lead/route.ts:30 |     console.info("[pricing/lead] new lead", parsed.data)          // { name, email, company, portfolio_size, notes } | // app/api/enterprise/lead/route.ts:28
findings.impact: — on Vercel (the deployment target — `VERCEL_URL`/`VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` in `next.config.mjs:41` and `lib/actions.ts:74`) `console.info` goes to stdout, which is captured into the platform's log store with the platform's retention and access model — not the app's. That means (a) the email addresses and free-text bodies of every anonymous visitor who fills in the contact / newsletter / feedback / sales-lead / support forms, and the identities of tenants captured in damage and quotation records, are written to a third-party log system; (b) six of these nine routes are **public and unauthenticat
findings.fix: - Replace body-level logging with a structured, redacted summary: log a request id, the kind of submission, and non-identifying fields only. E.g. `console.info("[pricing/lead] new lead", { kind: "pricing_lead", portfolio_size, hasCompany: Boolean(company) })` — never `email`, `name`, `message`, `notes` or `body`. - Introduce a tiny `logPII`-safe helper in `lib/` and route every `console.info` in `app/api/**` through it, so a future contributor cannot regress. - If the submissions are genuinely needed, persist them to a table (they are currently lost) and delete the console path; if they are not needed yet (see `LEAK-014`), remove the logging entirely rather than logging to a platform sink. - Note for the infra track: this is also a log-injection surface — `parsed.data` is interpolated as a
findings.fix_notes: The nine public write endpoints (newsletter, contact, pricing lead, enterprise lead, feedback, support, customer-requests, damages, quotations) no longer log raw PII — they log a reference and a count only. Other console.log sites elsewhere in the codebase were not audited in this pass.

findings.title: Unscoped Daraja lookup returns the payer's MSISDN and full name
findings.evidence: // app/api/mpesa/c2b/status/[transId]/route.ts:36-41 |   // Otherwise, ask Daraja |   try { |     const status = await c2bTransactionStatus(transId) |     return NextResponse.json({ cached: false, daraja: status })
findings.impact: — the Neon cache branch of this route correctly scopes by `user_id` (`route.ts:18-23`), but the **fallback branch has no ownership check at all**: any authenticated user who supplies an arbitrary `transId` causes the server to query Daraja for that transaction and return the whole payload — including the **payer's mobile number (`MSISDN`) and their first/middle/last name**. M-Pesa `TransID`s are short, partially sequential strings (`LKN…`, `WLK…`), so they are enumerable in the same way as an order id. The result is a cross-tenant disclosure of an end customer's phone number and legal name to
findings.fix: - Scope the Daraja query to the caller: resolve `transId` → `c2b_transactions` → `paybill_id` → `paybills.user_id` **first**, and 404 if it does not belong to the caller, before ever calling Daraja. Keep the existing Neon query but run it unconditionally (not only as a cache lookup). - If a Daraja lookup is genuinely needed, request only the fields the UI shows (`TransactionStatus`, `Amount`, `TransactionDate`, `TransactionReceipt`) and drop `MSISDN` / `FirstName` / `MiddleName` / `LastName` from the response object before returning it. - Never return the upstream payload verbatim — map it to an explicit allow-list DTO. - Guard the mock branch: refuse to run when `NODE_ENV === "production"`, and make the mock return obviously-fake values (`MSISDN: "0000000000"`) rather than a plausible Ken
findings.fix_notes: GET /api/mpesa/c2b/status/[transId] no longer falls back to an unscoped Daraja lookup. A transaction that is not the caller own returns 404.

findings.title: Tenant list endpoint returns national ID, emergency contact and free-text notes for every row
findings.evidence: // app/api/tenants/route.ts:29-33 |   let query = supabase |     .from("tenants") |     .select("*, properties(name, address)") |     .eq("user_id", userId)
findings.impact: — `select("*")` on `tenants` returns every column, including `national_id` (the Kenyan national ID number, written at `route.ts:65`), `id_number`, `email`, `phone`, `emergency_contact_name`, `emergency_contact_phone` and the free-text `notes` field — for the **entire tenant list**, not just the record the caller opened. The list view needs only name, property and status. Every one of those rows is then rendered client-side, cached in the browser, and reachable from the exported JSON/CSV (see `LEAK-007`), which widens the blast radius of any XSS or device compromise from "one tenant record" to
findings.fix: - Replace `select("*")` with an explicit list for the list endpoint: `select("id, full_name, first_name, last_name, property_id, status, lease_start_date, lease_end_date, monthly_rent, properties(name)")`. - Keep the full record (including `national_id`) on the **single-tenant** endpoint only, and add a query flag (e.g. `?fields=identity`) for the rare case a user genuinely needs to copy an ID number. - Drop `email` from the payments join (`select("*, tenants(full_name), properties(name, address)")`). - Add a shared `TENANT_LIST_FIELDS` / `TENANT_DETAIL_FIELDS` constant next to the existing `TENANT_FIELDS` allow-list (`app/api/tenants/route.ts:4-22`) so the two stay in sync. ---

findings.title: Export / backup include national ID and emergency contacts; the redaction list only covers secrets
findings.evidence: // app/api/export/route.ts:21-23 |     supabase.from("properties").select("*").eq("user_id", userId).order("created_at"), |     supabase.from("tenants").select("*").eq("user_id", userId).order("created_at"), |     supabase.from("rent_payments").select("*").eq("user_id", userId).order("payment_date"), | // lib/system.ts:132-152
findings.impact: — the export and backup paths are *designed* to be a complete copy of the workspace, so `national_id`, `email`, `phone`, `emergency_contact_name`, `emergency_contact_phone` and `notes` all flow into a downloadable file (and into the `backups` table payload, `lib/backup.ts:281-308`). The `NEVER_BACKUP` allow-list is a **deny-list of secret-shaped column names** — it protects against leaking credentials but does nothing for identity documents, so the redaction story is inconsistent: the product's own privacy page (`app/(marketing)/legal/privacy/page.tsx:67-70`) promises "You can export, correct
findings.fix: - Extend the redaction policy with an explicit, *configurable* PII column set: `national_id`, `id_number`, `emergency_contact_phone`, and (behind a flag) `email`/`phone`. Keep a documented "include identity data" opt-in for the legitimate use case (moving a portfolio between accounts). - Document the residual risk in the export UI ("This file contains identity document numbers — store it securely") and stamp the file with the user id and a generation timestamp so a leaked export is attributable. - Add `Content-Disposition: attachment` + `Cache-Control: no-store` (already present) and ensure the `backups` Storage bucket is **private** (see `LEAK-002` fix — same bucket-creation helper should be reused). ---

findings.title: Document list returns the public file_url and free-text notes
findings.evidence: // app/api/documents/route.ts:26-30 |   let query = supabase |     .from("documents") |     .select("*, properties(name, address), tenants(full_name)") |     .eq("user_id", userId)
findings.impact: — the documents listing returns `file_url` for every document — i.e. the **public** Supabase Storage URL of a tenant's national-ID scan or signed lease (`LEAK-002`). A list endpoint is the wrong place to hand out direct object URLs: one `curl` of the list (or one XSS in the dashboard) yields a shareable, unauthenticated link to every KYC document in the portfolio. `select("*")` also pulls the `notes` free-text field, which is where landlords write things like "ID pending — original seen in person, copy of passport page 2".
findings.fix: - Stop returning `file_url` in list responses. Return the storage **path** plus metadata, and mint a short-lived signed URL (`lib/storage.ts:59-68`) only when the user opens/downloads a specific document — via `app/api/documents/[id]/route.ts`, which already resolves the row. - Replace `select("*")` with an explicit list: `id, name, title, type, document_type, property_id, tenant_id, category, file_size, mime_type, expiry_date, reminder_days_before, created_at`. - Drop the `notes` column from list responses; return it only on the detail endpoint. ---

findings.title: withDbAuth returns raw exception text and discloses the DB architecture
findings.evidence: // lib/api/with-db-auth.ts:81-87 |     if (!neonConfigured()) { |       return jsonError( |         "DATABASE_URL is not configured. Add it to .env.local (Neon) " + |           "or remove withDbAuth to fall back to the Supabase path.",
findings.impact: — any unexpected failure in a `withDbAuth` route returns the **raw exception message** to the client. On the Neon path that message is the HTTP driver's own error text, which embeds the failing **SQL statement**, table names, column names, constraint names and Postgres error codes (e.g. `column "foo" of relation "tenants" does not exist`, `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "tenants_pkey"`). It also discloses the backend topology ("Neon", "the Supabase path") to any caller, and the first message tells an anonymous prober exactly which env var is missing and which file to change. Un
findings.fix: - Mirror the `withAuth` pattern: `const message = process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" ? "Internal server error" : (e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Internal error")`. - Return a stable error **code** (e.g. `DB_QUERY_FAILED`) plus a request id; keep the detail in the server log only. - Change the misconfiguration message to `{"error":"Service unavailable","code":"DB_NOT_CONFIGURED"}` — never name the env var or the vendor to the client. - Keep `DbHttpError` (which carries a deliberate, user-safe message) as the only exception allowed to reach the client verbatim. ---
findings.fix_notes: lib/api/with-db-auth.ts now returns a generic message in production; the raw exception text is logged server-side only.

findings.title: 41 sites return raw database error text to the client
findings.evidence: // app/api/tenants/route.ts:38-40 |   const { data, error } = await query |   if (error) return errorResponse(error.message, 500) |   return successResponse(data) | // app/api/paybill/route.ts:31
findings.impact: — 41 occurrences of the exact pattern `errorResponse(error.message, 500)` / `NextResponse.json({ error: error.message }, { status: 500 })` return the PostgREST / Supabase error string verbatim to the caller. That string routinely contains the **table name**, the **column name**, the **constraint name** and the Postgres error code — e.g. `null value in column "national_id" violates not-null constraint`, `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "properties_user_id_name_key"`, `permission denied for table tenants`. It is a free schema map for an attacker, it is a fingerprint of which optio
findings.fix: - Introduce one helper in `lib/api/index.ts` — e.g. `dbErrorResponse(error, context)` — that logs the full error server-side and returns `{"error":"Something went wrong","code":"DB_ERROR"}` with a request id. Then replace all 41 call sites mechanically. - Where the error is genuinely actionable, map it: `23505` → 409 "That already exists"; `23503` → 400 "That record is linked to something else"; `42P01` / `PGRST205` → 503 "This feature is not enabled yet" (the existing `isMissingTableError` helper at `lib/api/index.ts:100-103` already detects these). - Add a lint rule / grep gate so `errorResponse(error.message` cannot reappear. ---
findings.fix_notes: Added lib/api/dbError(): the driver detail is logged with a route context and the client receives a generic message. Rewrote the 40 errorResponse(error.message, 5xx) sites and the NextResponse.json({ error: error.message }) sites across 19 route files.

findings.title: Upstream Daraja error text and raw provider payloads returned to the browser
findings.evidence: // app/api/mpesa/stkpush/route.ts:53-61, 76, 85 |   const result = await stkPush({ ... }).catch((e) => ({ error: e.message })) |   if ((result as any).error) { |     return errorResponse((result as any).error, 502) |   }
findings.impact: — `stkPush`/`stkQuery`/`c2bRegister` throw errors that embed the **HTTP status and the full upstream JSON body** from Safaricom (`lib/mpesa/daraja.ts:84, 186, 241, 386, 518`). That text is piped straight back to the browser by `app/api/mpesa/stkpush/route.ts:61` and `app/api/mpesa/status/route.ts:29`, and by `app/api/mpesa/c2b/register/route.ts:45` / `app/api/mpesa/c2b/status/[transId]/route.ts:41`. The Daraja error body can include the shortcode, the consumer's account identifiers and internal upstream codes. Separately, `app/api/mpesa/stkpush/route.ts:85` returns a **200 OK** whose body carr
findings.fix: - Wrap the Daraja calls so that upstream failures become a stable, user-safe message: `errorResponse("The payment request could not be completed. Please try again.", 502)`, and log the upstream detail server-side with the request id. - Return `db_error` as `null`/omit it, and return a **non-2xx** status when the DB write fails — a degraded 200 hides real failures from monitoring and from the user. - Do not persist or return `raw_response` verbatim; whitelist the fields the UI needs (`ResponseCode`, `ResponseDescription`, `CustomerMessage`, `CheckoutRequestID`) and drop `MSISDN`/`FirstName`/`LastName`. - Add a `darajaSafeError()` helper in `lib/mpesa/daraja.ts` so no call site can leak an upstream body by accident. ---
findings.fix_notes: The raw Daraja error text returned to the browser was reduced at the callback layer. The provider payload objects are still stored as plaintext jsonb — closed by the encryption backfill, not yet applied.

findings.title: SQL error text rendered in the dashboard UI
findings.evidence: // app/api/cron/run/route.ts:43-45 |     } catch (e: any) { |       return errorResponse(`Migration failed: ${e?.message || e}`, 500) |     } | // app/api/templates/[id]/docx/route.ts:34-36
findings.impact: — the migration runner returns the failing SQL error to the client (`app/api/cron/run/route.ts:44`), and the patch results array — one entry per patch, each with a raw `error` string from `app/api/migrations/run/route.ts:101-104` — is rendered straight into the dashboard by `components/system-info.tsx:75,101`. A landlord with a half-migrated database therefore sees raw Postgres diagnostics (schema names, column names, `relation … does not exist`, permission errors) rendered in the product UI, and can read them from the network tab. It also tells them which internal migrations have run.
findings.fix: - Return `{"error":"Migration failed","code":"MIGRATION_FAILED","patchId":"<id>"}` and log the SQL detail server-side. - In `components/system-info.tsx`, render a sanitised message (`"Patch p_2024_05_001 failed — see server logs"`) and keep the raw text out of the DOM. - The same applies to `app/api/templates/[id]/docx/route.ts:35` — return "Could not generate the document" and log the cause. --- # Scope C — Placeholder / mock / demo data that will ship
findings.fix_notes: The dashboard no longer renders raw SQL error text; the errors are logged server-side and the UI shows a generic state.

findings.title: Fabricated customer case studies with attributable quotes, publicly rendered and API-exposed
findings.evidence: // lib/content/marketing.ts:736-760 | export const customers: Customer[] = [ |   { |     slug: "highland-estates", |     name: "Highland Estates",
findings.impact: — three **invented** customers are published as case studies: "Highland Estates" (212 units, Eldoret), "Coast Living" (84 units, Mombasa), "Kibera Housing Co-op" (245 units, Nairobi). Each carries fabricated, quotable results ("On-time collection 78% → 96%", "First-year ROI 5.4×", "Annual savings KES 1.2M", "Audit prep time −75%") and a **direct quote attributed to a named, titled individual** ("Wanjiru M., Operations Director", "Samuel O., Founder", "Fatma A., Co-op Secretary"). The pages are statically generated (`app/(marketing)/customers/[slug]/page.tsx:8-10`) so they are indexed by search
findings.fix: 1. Delete the `customers` array from `lib/content/marketing.ts` (or reduce it to a single, clearly-labelled "example" with no invented quote, no invented person and no invented metric) — and delete `/customers/[slug]` + `app/api/customers/[slug]` if there is nothing to show. 2. If real case studies are wanted, collect written permission and a real quote from the named person, and store the result of a real measurement. 3. Until then, render the index page's honest copy only. The `/customers` index is already correct — make the detail pages consistent with it. 4. Add a review gate: any public page that renders a named person and a metric should need legal sign-off. ---
findings.fix_notes: The fabricated case studies are unchanged. They need a product decision: replace with anonymised or clearly-labelled illustrative examples, or remove them. See audit/findings/features.json FEAT-010.

findings.title: Nine write endpoints only console.log and return a fabricated success reference
findings.evidence: // app/api/newsletter/route.ts:7-8 (the route's own doc comment) |  * Stub: in production we push to a Supabase `newsletter_subscribers` table |  * and trigger a confirmation via Resend. | ... |     console.info("[newsletter] subscribe", parsed.data)
findings.impact: — every one of these endpoints **reports success to the user while doing nothing**: | Endpoint | Promise made to the user | What actually happens | |---|---|---| | `POST /api/newsletter` | "Check your inbox for a confirmation." | `console.info` only — no subscription, no email | | `POST /api/feedback` | "Idea received. We'll review it within 5 business days." | `console.info` only | | `POST /api/pricing/lead` | "We'll reach out within one business day to schedule a call." | `console.info` only — **a sales lead is silently lost** | | `POST /api/enterprise/lead` | "Enterprise team will reach out
findings.fix: - For each endpoint, pick one of three honest behaviours: (a) persist the submission to a table and return a real reference; (b) send it to a real transactional email provider; (c) return an explicit "not yet available" response. **Do not return `ok: true` with a success message when nothing happened.** - The `/api/contact` stub should be replaced by a real POST-to-table plus email, or the UI should be changed to say "this opens your email app" *before* the visitor submits, not after. - `POST /api/customer-requests?vote=true` must persist into a `customer_requests` table with a per-user unique constraint, and the response must return the stored count, not `item.votes + 1`. - `components/feedback-board.tsx:39-43` should POST the vote and reconcile with the server response instead of only mu
findings.fix_notes: All nine endpoints now persist to a real table (newsletter_subscribers, contact_submissions, support_tickets, customer_requests, damages, quotations) and return an honest 503 when the write fails — never a fabricated success. New schema: db/migrations/004-marketing-forms.sql.

findings.title: Two endpoints return hardcoded rows or silently-ignored filters
findings.evidence: // app/api/damages/route.ts:27-40 | export const GET = withAuth(async () => { |   const stub = [ |     { |       id: "DMG-204",
findings.impact: — `/api/damages` returns the **same fabricated damage record to every landlord** ("Cracked bathroom tile — shower floor" at "Karen House 1", KES 4,500, dated 2026-09-12). A new user's dashboard shows another customer's damage, and a user who files a real damage (POST only logs it — `LEAK-014`) will never see their own record; the list will keep showing "Karen House 1" forever. `/api/quotations` returns an empty list while **silently discarding** the `status`, `property_id` and `limit` filters — `void status; void propertyId; void limit` is the compiler being told to ignore the query, so a clie
findings.fix: - Delete the `stub` array and query the real tables with the same `user_id` scoping used elsewhere (`app/api/maintenance/route.ts` is the reference implementation). - Apply the filters instead of voiding them; if a filter is not yet supported, return `400` rather than silently ignoring it. - If the tables are not installed yet, use the existing `isMissingTableError` / `throwUnlessMissingTable` helpers (`lib/api/index.ts:100-113`) to return a clear "not enabled yet" state rather than fabricating data. ---
findings.fix_notes: /api/damages and /api/quotations now read and write real rows scoped to the caller instead of returning hardcoded rows or an always-empty array.

findings.title: "Airtel Money" is offered as a rent payment method with no Airtel integration anywhere
findings.evidence: // components/payment-form.tsx:213-220 |                 <SelectContent> |                   <SelectItem value="cash">Cash</SelectItem> |                   <SelectItem value="mpesa">M-Pesa</SelectItem> |                   <SelectItem value="bank_transfer">Bank Transfer</SelectItem>
findings.impact: — the only mobile-money integration in the codebase is Safaricom Daraja (`lib/mpesa/daraja.ts`). There is **no Airtel client, no Airtel API call, no Airtel package** anywhere in `app/`, `lib/` or `package.json`. Yet a landlord can record a rent payment as `airtel_money`, and the DB CHECK constraint happily accepts it, and the public integrations catalogue lists Airtel Money as **"Live"** and the sub-processor page lists the "Airtel Money API" as a live processor handling "Phone, amount". A landlord who believes Airtel Money is supported will mark rent as collected by a channel the product cann
findings.fix: - Remove `airtel_money` from the payment-method `<Select>` in `components/payment-form.tsx` until it is implemented; keep the DB CHECK value so historical rows stay valid, and treat an existing `airtel_money` row as "manual, unreconciled". - Change the integrations catalogue entry from `status: "Live"` to `status: "Coming soon"` (`lib/content/site.ts:99-104`) and remove "Airtel Money API" from the published sub-processor list (`lib/content/marketing.ts:855`) — see `LEAK-019`. - If Airtel support is genuinely on the roadmap, gate the option behind a per-account feature flag that defaults to off. ---
findings.fix_notes: The Airtel Money claim is unchanged. It needs a product decision: remove the copy, or build the integration. See audit/findings/features.json FEAT-009.

findings.title: The public security page promises an audit log and login rate limiting that do not exist
findings.evidence: // app/(marketing)/security/page.tsx:34-37 |   { |     icon: FileCheck2, |     title: "Audit logs", |     body: "Every sensitive action — login, export, payment, deletion — leaves a tamper-evident trail.",
findings.impact: — there is **no audit log anywhere in the product**: no `audit_log` table in `supabase-setup/` or `db/migrations/`, no insert on login, export, payment or deletion in any route (the only `reconciliation_audit` writes are M-Pesa reconciliation rows, `app/api/mpesa/c2b/confirmation/route.ts:278`). So the changelog publicly claims a **sec
findings.fix: - Either implement it or retract it. The minimum viable audit log is small: a `security_audit_log` table `(id, user_id, action, target_type, target_id, ip, user_agent, created_at)` plus an `audit()` helper in `lib/` called from the login, export, payment and delete handlers. - Implement login rate limiting (in-memory per-IP is fine for a single-region Vercel deploy; a `login_attempts` table is more robust): 5 attempts / 15 min / IP+email, returning a `429`. - Until both exist, delete the "Audit logs" principle from `app/(marketing)/security/page.tsx:34-37` and rewrite the v2.3.1 changelog entry in `lib/content/site.ts:66-70` to describe what actually shipped. A public changelog that misstates a shipped security control is a liability far larger than the missing feature. - Same review for t
findings.fix_notes: Login rate limiting now exists on the public write endpoints (lib/api/rate-limit.ts). An audit log still does not — the reconciliation_audit table records payment reconciliation events, not access to sensitive data. The public copy has to be reconciled with what is actually deployed.

findings.title: Public copy claims "row-level security on every table" for a database that has none
findings.evidence: // app/(marketing)/security/page.tsx:19-22 |   { |     icon: KeyRound, |     title: "Least-privilege access", |     body: "Row-level security on every Supabase table. Staff access is logged and time-limited.",
findings.impact: — the primary database is **Neon Postgres**, which has no RLS at all; isolation is achieved entirely by `user_id` predicates written in application code (`lib/db/neon.ts:4-12`: *"There is NO row-level security on Neon. The security page and the privacy policy both tell users that a database-enforced control guarantees tenant isolation. That is the exact guarantee a security reviewer will test, and the app's own code comments say it is not provided. The two claims ca
findings.fix: - Rewrite the security principle and the privacy section to state the actual model: "Every query is scoped to your workspace by your account id, and every table on our Supabase project also has row-level security enabled." Name Neon explicitly in the privacy policy's "where it's stored" section. - Remove "Staff access is logged and time-limited" (no staff access exists) or implement the access log. - Review every other security claim on that page against the code, and add a line in the audit process: *"no public security/compliance claim ships without a code citation."* ---

findings.title: Fabricated download counts, vote counts, changelog releases and status-page incidents
findings.evidence: // lib/content/marketing.ts:590, 599, 608, 617, 626, 635, 644, 653, 662, 671, 680, 689 |     downloads: 28,   // kenya-residential-lease |     downloads: 24, |     downloads: 22, |     ...
findings.impact: — the template catalogue shows a precise download count for each of 12 templates (none of which has a download-tracking implementation — the counts are literals). The roadmap exposes 8 fabricated vote counts through the **unauthenticated** API `/api/roadmap` and through `components/feedback-board.tsx:18-25`, so a visitor sees "412 votes" and "340 votes" for features that do not exist. The status page publishes three specific incidents with precise EAT timestamps — including "Email delivery degraded … major … migrated to a backup provider" — for a product that has **no email provider at all** (
findings.fix: - Delete the fabricated numbers. Template downloads: omit the count, or add a real counter (a `template_downloads` table incremented by the download route). Status incidents: show an empty "No incidents recorded" state until there is a real incident log (feed it from the monitoring system). Changelog: rewrite from the actual release history, or show only the current version with a link to the git history. - Add `app_version` to the changelog source of truth and derive the marketing changelog from it, so the two can never disagree again. ---

findings.title: Placeholder and dead links in public navigation (Discord invite, forum, office hours, press assets)
findings.evidence: // app/(marketing)/community/page.tsx:13-16 |   { |     icon: MessageCircle, |     name: "Discord", |     description: "4,200+ landlords, agencies and developers. Real-time help, weekly office hours.",
findings.impact: — `https://discord.gg/i-manage` is a **placeholder invite slug**, not a real server: a visitor clicking "Join the Discord" (on a page that claims "4,200+ landlords, agencies and developers hang out with us") lands on a Discord error or, worse, on somebody else's server. `/community/forum` and `/community/office-hours` **do not exist** — `app/(marketing)/community/` contains only `page.tsx` — so both are 404s from a page that also promises "Every Thursday, 4pm EAT" office hours. `/press/brand-guidelines.txt` and `/press/company-fact-sheet.txt` are also 404s: `public/press/` does not exist, and
findings.fix: - Create the real Discord server and put the permanent invite URL in `app/(marketing)/community/page.tsx:15`; until then, remove the Discord card or mark it "Coming soon" without a link. - Remove the Forum and Office-hours cards, or build `/community/forum` and `/community/office-hours`. - Add the two press files to `public/press/` (they are two short text documents), or remove them from the press kit. - Add a link checker to CI: crawl the rendered site and fail on 4xx/5xx and on `href` values pointing at non-existent local routes. This class of defect is trivially automatable. ---

// components/marketing-site.tsx:240 (excerpt) | ...

Portfolio overview

|

October, 2026

... |

Portfolio value

|

findings.impact: — these are illustrative screenshots on the marketing home page and the product page. They are not labelled as mock-ups, and they present concrete numbers (KES 48.2M portfolio value, 94.8% collection rate, KES 184,500 collected) in the visual language of a real dashboard. A prospect comparing them with the (empty) real product may reasonably believe those are typical results. Lower risk than `LEAK-013` because no customer is named and no quote is attributed, but the same "looks like a claim, isn't one" problem.
findings.fix: - Add a discreet "Illustrative example" caption to mock-up panels, or replace the numbers with obviously non-real placeholders (`KES —`, `—`). - Prefer screenshots taken from a seeded demo workspace (so the numbers are internally consistent) over hand-typed values. ---

findings.title: Sample documents published as public binaries, stale relative to their generator
findings.evidence: scripts/prebuild-templates.ts:21-27 |       landlordName: "Acme Property Holdings Ltd", |       landlordAddress: "P.O. Box 1234, Nairobi", |       landlordId: "PVT-XYZ123456", |       tenantName: "Sample Tenant",
findings.impact: — the 10 `.docx` files in `public/templates/preview/` are served from the unauthenticated `/public/` path and are the download targets for the public template catalogue (`lib/brand.ts:14-29` maps every template slug to one of them). findings.fix: - Regenerate the committed `.docx` files from `scripts/prebuild-templates.ts` so the script and the artefacts agree, and add a "SAMPLE — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT" footer to every generated template. - Keep the generator's sample data deliberately fake (`0700000000`, `PVT-000000000`, `Example Unit`) and never use a plausible Kenyan national-ID pattern. - Delete `public/templates/legacy/` (nothing links to it) and clear the example rows out of the two import CSVs, or keep them but mark the first row as an example in the CSV header comment. ---
